one_liner: CLI CSV toolkit with a SIMD parser and built-in expression language; faster single-threaded select than xsv, Polars, DuckDB.
what_it_does: xan is a command-line tool for filtering, slicing, aggregating, joining, and previewing CSV files directly from the shell, plus converting to/from JSON, Excel, Parquet, and numpy and handling CSV-adjacent formats (.cdx, .vcf, .gtf). It is not a library API: it is a standalone binary with xsv-style subcommands (select, count, join, stats, view, ...) and its own "moonblade" expression language for row-level transforms, avoiding the need to shell out to Python/Lua for computed columns. It began as a fork of BurntSushi's xsv but the README says it has been nearly entirely rewritten.
how_it_is_fast: Core parsing goes through medialab/simd-csv, a separate SIMD-accelerated CSV parser crate, instead of a byte-at-a-time scalar reader like the csv crate xsv uses. Selected commands (e.g. the `parallel` subcommand and some stats/aggregation paths) multithread across cores. The moonblade expression language is evaluated directly by xan rather than by invoking an external scripting interpreter, cutting subprocess/interpreter overhead for row transforms.
when_to_use: Ad hoc CLI exploration and filtering of large (GB-TB) CSV files where you'd otherwise reach for xsv or csvkit
Unquoted or sparsely-quoted CSV where single-threaded select/count throughput matters (fastest single-threaded tool in the zsv shootout)
Want stats, join, dedup, pivot, and format conversion in one CLI without leaving the shell for pandas/DuckDB
Converting CSV to/from JSON, ndjson, Excel, Parquet, or numpy from the command line
Already scripting with xsv and want a faster, more feature-rich drop-in CLI replacement
when_not_to_use: Need an embeddable Rust/Python library rather than a CLI binary; not documented as an embeddable API (use simd-csv or the csv crate directly instead)
Data contains nonstandard-quoted CSV; xan produces incorrect output there per the wave3 verification pass
Need the single fastest option regardless of thread count: zsv fast/compat with --parallel and DuckDB with QUOTE='' beat xan on the same benchmark
Need a build with documented, reproducible compiler flags; the benchmarked xan binary's flags are unstated (evidence tier C)
Want a minimal, small dependency footprint; xan bundles 60+ crates including Excel, Parquet, HTML, and Markdown parsers

integration.form: crate (binary via cargo install; not designed as an embeddable library)
integration.dependencies: 60+ crates, including ahash, aho-corasick, csv, calamine (Excel), comrak (Markdown), docopt, jiff, and medialab/simd-csv for the fast CSV path
integration.platforms: x86_64 (Linux gnu/musl, macOS, Windows msvc), aarch64 (macOS, Linux gnu); ppc64le only via unofficial conda-forge build, not CI-built
integration.thread_safety: not documented as a library API; CLI exposes an explicit `parallel` subcommand for multithreaded batch runs
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: CLI-compatible successor to xsv's command style and originally forked from it, but nearly entirely rewritten and not an API-level drop-in

gotchas: Produces incorrect output on nonstandard-quoted CSV, the same limitation zsv-fast has (per wave3 verifier notes)
Cargo.toml licenses it "Unlicense OR MIT" (dual), though the catalog record lists Unlicense only
The competitive benchmark numbers come from rival project zsv's own shootout script, not from xan's own README or docs
Large dependency surface (Excel, Parquet, HTML, Markdown parsing all bundled) makes this a heavyweight binary, not a minimal tool
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick xan over qsv, zsv, or DuckDB/Polars when you want one feature-rich CLI (stats, join, expression language, multi-format conversion) rather than the single fastest parser; pick zsv (especially --parallel) or DuckDB's QUOTE='' path instead when raw select/count throughput is the only goal, and pick simd-csv directly if you want the SIMD parser as a Rust library dependency rather than a CLI tool.
verified_claims_summary: On zsv's own darwin-arm64 shootout (Apple M3 Pro, xan 0.54.1, csv crate-based xsv as baseline, 500000x20-row unquoted/sparse-quoted data, best-of-5), xan's `select` ran 0.077s/0.081s versus xsv's 0.189s/0.195s (~2.4x), beating single-threaded Polars (0.410s/0.408s) and default DuckDB v0.10.2 (0.110s/0.105s), but losing to zsv fast/compat in --parallel mode and to DuckDB with QUOTE='' on sparse-quoted data; the xan binary's compiler flags are not stated.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-23, 4.5k stars) and Unlicense-licensed per the catalog record (Cargo.toml also permits MIT), so it is safe to install via cargo/brew/pacman/nix — but it ships as a CLI tool, not a library, so "copyable" usability applies to its command surface rather than embedding its source.
